Remember the Persians were montheists. They believed in good and evil, specifically Asher and the Jews. The Bible began to reflect Persian beliefs, especially in the idea of eschatology (end of the world). According to Jewish belief, they are not afraid of the Romans because eventually the Messiah will return to lead them to war against the Romans. Because the Messiah is anointed by God, they believe they will triumph.

So the Jews wait for the Messiah of war to reclaim the Davidic kingdom. Paul uses eschatology cleverly; he says Jesus is not the Messiah of war but the Messiah of peace. Therefore, the Jews should not resist the Romans.

The second major culture that Paul uses is Greek culture. The Greeks have mystery schools, which are cults and will become secret societies today. One such school worships Dionysus, the god of creativity and wine. Dionysus is born of a virgin mother and killed by enemies of Zeus but resurrected by him.

In these mystery schools, worshippers believe they eat the body of Dionysus during a ritual meal, absorbing his energy and becoming one with him through communion. Christians have the same ritual, called eucharist or thanksgiving.

The third major culture is Roman. The social structure is the patria potestas, where a patriarch at the top has children and slaves in a hierarchical system. Promising slaves are freed to become clients, creating a business empire. Paul uses this model for his church, mirroring it with bishops and disciples.

This switch from traditional systems to Paul's new church solves the problem of slave obedience by offering eternal salvation. Slaves now work harder to earn their place in heaven, making them more obedient and productive.
